screening_decisions.reason: This is a review article summarizing literature on drug-induced liver injury. It is not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment.
This study investigates aspirin absorption during migraine attacks, not paracetamol. The intervention does not match the selection criteria.
This is an observational study analyzing time trends for paracetamol suicides and overdoses. Not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a Cochrane systematic review about aspirin for migraine, not a primary RCT of paracetamol.

This appears to be a randomized controlled trial comparing paracetamol alone, DHE alone, and combination therapy with placebo. The study includes 288 patients with migraine attacks and tests paracetamol as a treatment. Conservative approach to include for further review.
This is a population-based epidemiological survey about headache prevalence. Not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a methodological paper about assessing quality of clinical trial reports. Not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis of cross-over trials. Not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a systematic review/meta-analysis of pharmacological treatments for migraine. Not a primary RCT of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a population-based telephone survey about headache prevalence. Not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is an epidemiological study analyzing migraine prevalence patterns. Not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial that includes paracetamol 500mg as a treatment arm. The study has 1743 patients and tests treatment of migraine attacks. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a review article about the mechanism of action of paracetamol. Not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a methodological chapter from a book about assessing risk of bias. Not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a methodological paper about developing a database of RCTs. Not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine.

This is a randomized, double-blind, three-way cross-over trial comparing paracetamol 1g alone vs paracetamol + domperidone. The study has 46 patients with migraine and tests self-administered paracetamol. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper about calculating confidence intervals. Not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a methodological paper about pain intensity scales. Not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine.

This is a randomized, double-blind, crossover phase III clinical trial comparing paracetamol 1000mg vs etodolac for acute migraine treatment. The study has 229 adult patients with migraine and tests self-administered paracetamol. Meets all selection criteria.
This study investigates aspirin absorption during migraine attacks with metoclopramide. Does not involve paracetamol as the intervention.
Literature review on paracetamol poisoning and pack size legislation. Not a clinical trial on migraine treatment.

Randomised crossover trial comparing domperidone+paracetamol vs sumatriptan in migraine. Meets population/intervention criteria. Included conservatively despite blinding not explicitly stated in abstract.
IV metoclopramide monotherapy in ED. No paracetamol. Not self-administered.
Methodological paper on meta-analysis. Not a primary clinical trial.
Economic study on cost of headache disorders. Not a clinical trial.
Double-blind, crossover trial comparing Midrin (contains acetaminophen) vs acetaminophen alone vs placebo. Meets all criteria including sample size.
Survey on treatment patterns. Not a randomized controlled trial.
Mechanism of action study (prostaglandin synthetase). Not a clinical trial.
Pharmacokinetics study in 5 volunteers. Not a migraine treatment trial. Sample size too small.
Review article on diagnosis of migraine. Not a clinical trial.
Review/commentary on COX-3 mechanism. Not a clinical trial.
Abstract describes fungal infection study. Irrelevant topic.
Global Burden of Disease epidemiological study. Not a clinical trial.
Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial of acetaminophen 1000mg vs placebo for migraine. Meets all criteria.
Systematic review on paracetamol safety in alcoholics. Not a primary trial on migraine efficacy.
Survey on patient preferences. Not a clinical trial.
Commentary on Global Burden of Disease survey. Not a clinical trial.
Methodological study on duplicate publication. Not a paracetamol migraine trial.
Review article on paracetamol hepatotoxicity. Not a clinical trial.
Trial of metoclopramide vs sumatriptan. No paracetamol intervention.

This is an epidemiological cross-sectional survey studying prevalence of headache disorders in Russia. It does not test paracetamol as an intervention for acute migraine treatment. No randomized controlled trial design.
This is a systematic review of epidemiological studies on headache prevalence in Europe. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a randomized, double-blind, crossover study comparing tolfenamic acid with paracetamol (500mg and 1000mg doses) for treating common migraine attacks. 83 patients were admitted, with 70 completing 4 attacks and 58 completing all 8 attacks. Paracetamol was used as an active comparator to treat acute migraine episodes, meeting all selection criteria.

This is a longitudinal survey study evaluating economic burden and healthcare resource utilization in transformed migraine. It is not a randomized controlled trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.
This is a clinical practice guideline based on expert consensus and literature review. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.
This is an overview of epidemiological evidence on migraine burden and disability measurement. It is not a randomized controlled trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a before-and-after observational study evaluating the impact of legislation on paracetamol/salicylate overdose mortality and morbidity. It does not test paracetamol efficacy for acute migraine treatment and is not a randomized controlled trial.

This is a double-blind controlled study of Paramax (paracetamol 0.5g + metoclopramide 5mg) versus placebo for acute migraine treatment. 49 patients entered the study. This tests paracetamol combined with an antiemetic (metoclopramide), which aligns with the review objective of paracetamol with or without an antiemetic. Sample size appears adequate (>10 per arm).
This is a qualitative systematic literature review and recommendations paper. While it discusses acetaminophen/paracetamol for migraine, it is not a primary randomized controlled trial.
This is a basic science/molecular biology study describing COX-3 protein cloning and characterization. It is not a clinical trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with 4 groups: rizatriptan+acetaminophen, rizatriptan alone, acetaminophen alone, and placebo. 173 patients treated a migraine attack. Acetaminophen (paracetamol) 1000mg was tested both alone and in combination. This meets all selection criteria for testing paracetamol in acute migraine treatment.

This is a methodological/statistical paper discussing trial size requirements and random effects in clinical trials. It uses simulated data and pooled data from analgesic trials but is not itself a randomized controlled trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine.

This is a population-based survey study evaluating disability profiles and treatment patterns in chronic vs episodic migraine. It is observational, not a randomized controlled trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.
This is a narrative review of economic articles and perspectives on migraine burden and treatment. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a clinical practice guide/review article providing recommendations for migraine management. While it mentions paracetamol as a treatment option, it is not a primary randomized controlled trial.
This is a review article discussing the mechanism of action of acetaminophen/paracetamol and the potential role of COX-3. It is not a clinical trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is an epidemiological survey study assessing migraine prevalence and preventive therapy use patterns in the US population. It is not a randomized controlled trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a population-based survey study evaluating migraine recognition and treatment patterns in France. It is observational, not a randomized controlled trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing oral acetaminophen (paracetamol) 1000mg with placebo for treating single acute migraine attacks. Subjects met IHS diagnostic criteria for migraine. The study reports headache response rates, pain-free rates, and other outcomes at 2 hours. This clearly meets all selection criteria.

This is an economic/cross-sectional study quantifying direct medical costs of chronic vs episodic migraine in five European countries. It is not a randomized controlled trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This study investigates aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid/ASA) pharmacokinetics in migraine patients, not paracetamol (acetaminophen). The selection criteria explicitly require studies using self-administered paracetamol to treat migraine headache episodes. While this study does examine metoclopramide (an antiemetic) combined with oral medication in migraineurs, the primary analgesic agent is aspirin, which is outside the scope of this review focused on paracetamol. Additionally, the study measures pharmacokinetic parameters (absorption rates, plasma levels) rather than clinical efficacy outcomes for migraine treatment.
